name: Creamy Chicken & Mushroom Pie
blurb: Chicken, mushrooms and tarragon in a cream sauce under puff pastry.
ingredients: 30g butter, 30g flour, 400ml chicken stock, 100ml double cream
method: Brown the chicken, then set aside. Soften the onion, leeks and mushrooms in butter for 10 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then the stock, and simmer to a sauce. Add cream, tarragon, mustard and the chicken.
Tip into a pie dish and cool slightly. Top with pastry, seal, glaze with egg and cut a vent.
Bake at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes until puffed and deep golden.

name: Bacon Mac & Cheese
blurb: Baked macaroni in a three-cheese sauce with crispy bacon and a crumb top.
method: Fry the bacon until crisp. Cook the macaroni 2 minutes under and drain.
Make a roux with butter and flour, whisk in the milk and simmer to a smooth sauce.
Off the heat stir in the cheeses and mustard, then the pasta and bacon.
Tip into a dish, top with the panko and bake at 200C fan for 20 minutes.

name: Beef Stroganoff
blurb: Strips of beef and mushrooms in a mustard-soured cream sauce with rice.
method: Sear the beef in a very hot pan in batches, then set aside.
Soften the onion and mushrooms, add the paprika and mustard.
Add the stock and let it reduce, then stir in the soured cream and warm gently.
Return the beef and any juices, heat through, finish with parsley and serve with rice.

name: Sausage & Bean Casserole
blurb: Browned sausages braised with beans, tomatoes and smoked paprika.
ingredients: 2 x 400g tins mixed beans or cannellini, drained
Crusty bread or mash to serve
method: Brown the sausages all over in a casserole, then set aside.
Soften the onion and peppers, add the garlic, paprika and thyme.
Add the tomatoes, beans and Worcestershire, return the sausages, and simmer for 25-30 minutes.
Season and serve with bread or mash.

name: The Ultimate Fish Finger Sandwich
blurb: Homemade crumbed fish fingers in soft bread with tartare and lettuce.
ingredients: 400g chunky white fish, cut into fingers
Tartare: 4 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp chopped gherkin, 1 tsp capers, squeeze of lemon
method: Coat the fish in flour, egg then panko.
Shallow fry for 2-3 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked through. Drain.
Mix the tartare.
Build sandwiches with buttered bread, tartare, lettuce and the hot fish fingers.

name: Loaded Cauliflower Cheese
blurb: Whole roasted cauliflower florets in a sharp cheese sauce with a crunchy top.
ingredients: 1 tsp English mustard, pinch of nutmeg
30g pumpkin seeds or crushed crackers for the top
method: Roast the florets with a little oil at 220C fan for 20 minutes until edges char.
Make a white sauce with butter, cornflour and milk; off the heat stir in most of the cheese and the mustard.
Fold the cauliflower through the sauce in a dish, top with remaining cheese and the seeds.
Bake at 200C fan for 20 minutes until bubbling.

name: Beef Chilli Loaded Jacket Potatoes
blurb: Crisp-skinned baked potatoes stuffed with beef chilli, cheese and soured cream.
ingredients: 2 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tsp chipotle paste
400g tin chopped tomatoes, 400g tin kidney beans
150g grated cheddar, soured cream and spring onions to serve
method: Bake the pricked, oiled and salted potatoes at 200C fan for 70-80 minutes until crisp.
Brown the mince, add the onion, pepper and spices, then the tomatoes and beans. Simmer 30 minutes.
Split the potatoes, fluff with butter and season.
Load with chilli and cheese, return to the oven for 3 minutes, then top with soured cream and spring onions.

name: Tuna Pasta Bake
blurb: Pasta, tuna and sweetcorn in a cheesy tomato sauce with a golden crust.
method: Cook the pasta 2 minutes under.
Make a cheese sauce with butter, flour, milk, most of the cheese and the mustard, then stir in the passata.
Fold in the pasta, tuna and corn, tip into a dish, top with crumbs and the rest of the cheese.
Bake at 200C fan for 20-25 minutes until golden.

name: Cheesy-Topped Cottage Pie
blurb: Rich beef mince and vegetables under a cheddar-crusted mash.
ingredients: 1 tbsp Worcestershire, 350ml beef stock, 1 tsp thyme
900g potatoes for mash, 60g butter, splash of milk, 80g grated cheddar
method: Brown the mince, set aside. Soften the vegetables for 10 minutes.
Add the purée, Worcestershire and thyme, return the beef, add the stock and simmer 25 minutes. Stir in the peas.
Mash the boiled potatoes with butter and milk; season.
Top the mince with mash, fork the top, scatter with cheddar and bake at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes.

name: Proper Chicken Noodle Soup
blurb: Golden broth, shredded chicken, soft noodles and lots of parsley.
ingredients: Big handful of parsley, squeeze of lemon
method: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in a little oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic.
Pour in the stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the noodles and cook until tender, then stir in the chicken to heat through.
Finish with parsley, lemon and plenty of black pepper.

name: Cheesy Tomato Gnocchi Bake
blurb: Potato gnocchi baked in a rich tomato sauce with mozzarella and basil.
method: Fry the garlic and chilli in oil, add the purée, then the tomatoes and sugar. Simmer 15 minutes.
Boil the gnocchi until they float, then drain.
Fold the gnocchi through the sauce in an ovenproof pan, dot with mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake or grill at 220C for 10 minutes until blistered; finish with basil.

name: Corned Beef Hash with a Fried Egg
blurb: Crisp fried potato and onion with corned beef and a runny egg on top.
ingredients: Brown sauce or beans to serve
method: Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the potatoes and press down to crisp.
Turn, add the corned beef and Worcestershire, and keep frying until crisp in patches.
Fry the eggs.
Serve the hash topped with a fried egg and brown sauce or beans.

name: Roasted Vegetable Lasagne
blurb: Layers of roast Mediterranean veg, tomato sauce, béchamel and pasta.
ingredients: 2 aubergines, 2 courgettes, 2 peppers, 1 red onion, chopped and roasted
2 x 400g tins chopped tomatoes, 2 garlic cloves, handful of basil
60g butter, 60g flour, 700ml milk, pinch of nutmeg
method: Roast the vegetables with oil at 200C fan for 30 minutes.
Simmer the tomatoes with garlic and basil for 20 minutes.
Make a béchamel with butter, flour and milk; add nutmeg and half the cheese.
Layer tomato sauce, veg, pasta and béchamel, repeating, finishing with béchamel and cheese.
Bake at 190C fan for 35-40 minutes until golden. Rest 10 minutes.

name: Turkey Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
blurb: Light turkey meatballs simmered in a herby tomato sauce, with spaghetti.
ingredients: 1 small onion grated, 1 egg, 40g breadcrumbs, 1 tsp oregano, 2 garlic cloves
1 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tsp chilli flakes
method: Mix the mince with the onion, egg, breadcrumbs, oregano and garlic; roll into small balls.
Brown the meatballs in a pan, then set aside.
Fry the purée and chilli, add the tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes, then return the meatballs for 15 minutes.
Serve over spaghetti with basil.

name: Jacket Potato with Tuna Mayo & Sweetcorn
blurb: The classic quick fix — fluffy jacket, tuna mayo, corn and cheese.
method: Bake the pricked, oiled and salted potatoes at 200C fan for 70-80 minutes.
Mix the tuna with mayo, corn and spring onions.
Split the potatoes, fluff with butter and season.
Pile on the tuna mayo and scatter with cheese.

name: French Onion Pasta
blurb: Deeply caramelised onions, gruyère and stock tossed through pasta.
method: Cook the onions low and slow in the butter and oil for 35-40 minutes until deep brown; add the sugar near the end.
Add the wine and reduce, then the stock and thyme, and simmer 10 minutes.
Cook the pasta and toss through the onion sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Off the heat stir in the cheeses until glossy; season with black pepper.

name: Toad in the Hole with Onion Gravy
blurb: Sausages baked in crisp Yorkshire batter, drowned in onion gravy.
ingredients: Gravy: 2 onions sliced, 1 tbsp flour, 500ml beef stock, splash of Worcestershire
method: Whisk the flour, eggs and milk to a smooth batter and rest 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 220C fan. Put the fat and sausages in a roasting tin for 10 minutes until sizzling.
Pour in the batter and bake 25-30 minutes without opening the door, until risen and golden.
Caramelise the onions slowly, stir in the flour then the stock and Worcestershire, and simmer to a gravy.

name: Special Fried Rice
blurb: Day-old rice fried with prawns, char siu, egg, peas and spring onion.
ingredients: 150g char siu or cooked ham, diced
2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, white pepper
method: Scramble the eggs in a very hot oiled wok, then remove.
Fry the garlic and peas briefly, add the rice and press to heat through.
Add the prawns, ham, soy, sesame oil and white pepper, and toss.
Return the egg, fold through the spring onions and serve.
